metaDescription: Real 2026 Istanbul relocation budget covering upfront rent deposits, European vs Asian side rents, 54,258 TRY IMEI fee, Ikamet, and 90-day totals.
quickAnswer: Moving to Istanbul in 2026 requires substantial upfront cash beyond monthly rent. Signing a standard lease typically takes four months of rent—first month, a two-month deposit, and one month’s broker fee plus 20% VAT—alongside residence permit fees, private health insurance, utility deposits, and either the 54,258 TRY IMEI tax or a local phone.

body.text: How much upfront cash (deposit, 1st month, agency fee, Ikamet, insurance, furniture) does moving to Istanbul require?

For a mid-range apartment renting at 50,000–65,000 TRY monthly, expect 240,000 to 350,000 TRY ($5,500–$8,100) in Month 1 before furniture. Standard leases require first month’s rent, a one-to-two-month deposit (capped legally at three months), and a one-month broker commission plus 20% VAT.

Government residence permit (Ikamet) costs include the 2026 [residence permit card fee of 964 TRY](https://residencepermitinturkey.com/turkey-residence-permit-fees-2026.html) plus nationality-specific permit fees listed by the [Presidency of Migration Management](https://en.goc.gov.tr/documents-for-residence-permit-fee-amount). Mandatory private foreign health insurance runs roughly 12,000 to 35,000 TRY per adult annually depending on age, while furnishing an unfurnished 2+1 apartment with basic appliances and beds adds 140,000 to 250,000 TRY.
How do European-side vs Asian-side rents compare in 2026?

Istanbul’s citywide average apartment rent reached roughly [45,510 TRY per month in late 2026](https://www.imtilak.net/en/articles/apartment-rent-prices-turkey), with 100-square-meter units spanning about 22,800 TRY in outer districts like Esenyurt up to 65,100 TRY in central Kadıköy. Prime European-side neighborhoods such as Beşiktaş, Nişantaşı, and Cihangir typically command 15% to 30% premiums over comparable Asian-side flats in Ataşehir or Göztepe.

body.text: Always confirm whether your chosen neighborhood (mahalle) is open to new foreign residence permit registrations on the [Göç İdaresi residence permit portal](https://en.goc.gov.tr/residence-1) before signing a lease.
What hidden setup costs (notary, utility deposits, IMEI tax) surprise newcomers?

The largest shock for newcomers in 2026 is Türkiye’s foreign mobile phone IMEI registration tax, set at [54,258 TRY from January 1, 2026](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/business/turkiye-sets-2026-imei-registration-fee-for-phones-brought-from-abroad-at-1263-3212215). Foreign handsets work for [120 days on a Turkish SIM card](https://bayraktarattys.com/comprehensive-guide-to-registering-imported-phones-in-turkey) before network blocking, making a locally purchased mid-range Turkish smartphone cheaper for many expats than registering an older foreign device.

items: Notary & sworn translations: Budget 8,000 to 18,000 TRY for notarized lease contracts, passport translations, and apostilled marriage or birth certificates.
Utility deposits & connections: Electricity (CK Boğaziçi / Enerjisa), natural gas (İGDAŞ), water (İSKİ), and fiber internet setup deposits total roughly 10,000 to 18,000 TRY.
DASK earthquake insurance: Required before activating electricity or gas accounts in your name; typically 1,500 to 3,500 TRY per year.
Building dues (Aidat): Gated compounds with security and pools charge substantial monthly aidat separate from rent.

body.text: How much should a single expat vs family budget for Month 1–3?

Across the first 90 days—combining lease move-in cash, setup, Ikamet, insurance, groceries, transit, and utilities—a single expat renting a furnished 1+1 should budget $7,500 to $10,500. A family of three or four renting a larger gated-compound flat should budget $13,000 to $19,500, excluding international school tuition.

Holding 25% of your first-quarter budget in a liquid multi-currency buffer cushions Turkish lira exchange swings, initial hotel stays during apartment hunting, and unexpected notary or translation fees.

faq.q: Is a two-month security deposit legal in Istanbul?
faq.a: Yes. Under the Turkish Code of Obligations, residential landlords may request a security deposit up to a maximum of three months’ rent, though one to two months is standard in Istanbul.

faq.q: Can I avoid paying the 54,258 TRY IMEI registration fee in 2026?
faq.a: Yes. If you stay longer than 120 days, buying a locally registered smartphone from an authorized Turkish retailer avoids the 54,258 TRY foreign IMEI registration tax altogether.

faq.q: How much do real estate agents charge in Istanbul?
faq.a: Licensed brokers legally charge up to one month’s rent plus 20% VAT (equivalent to 1.2 months’ rent) as a one-time commission upon signing a residential lease.

faq.q: Do furnished Istanbul apartments save money in the first 90 days?
faq.a: Yes. Renting a furnished flat raises monthly rent by roughly 15% to 25%, but it eliminates 140,000 to 250,000 TRY in upfront furniture and appliance cash outlays during Month 1.

faq.q: Are all Istanbul neighborhoods open for new foreign Ikamet applications?
faq.a: No. Certain high-density neighborhoods (mahalle) are closed to new foreign residence registrations. Always verify the exact street address against current Göç İdaresi rules before paying a deposit.
